transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Zoe Alvarez (Redwood Partnerships); Carlos Ramirez, Anita Desai, Ravi Patel, Leah Wong (Constellation Cloud)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro, map of integration options, next steps to share docs and run pilot

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the partner team at Redwood. Ethan's our SE, Zoe's from partnerships. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Carlos Ramirez: Good thanks, Maya. Excited to chat — we've been looking at potential inference partners, curious about how Redwood could fit with our managed offering.
[00:14] Ethan Park: Great. Quick agenda — we'll do intros, run through Redwood's integration options (hosted API, dedicated pools, private/VPC), then talk ops: perf, security, and pilot next steps.
[00:24] Ravi Patel: Sounds good. To set context, Constellation runs a multi-tenant cloud for enterprise SaaS; we have both batch inference and latency-sensitive endpoints. Majority of our fleet is A100 and H100 across two regions. We also have some Ampere A2 instances for cost-sensitive workloads.
[00:40] Anita Desai: Yep, and our typical P99 target is 300-400ms for small generation calls; for larger chat workloads we target throughput more than single-call latency. We're interested in how Redwood handles KV cache and batching across GPUs.
[00:54] Ethan Park: Right — so Redwood's serving runtime does continuous batching and prefix KV caching. For private deployments we can tie into your network (VPC peering) and we do KMS integration for key encryption. Quick note: the transcript might say K-V cash in the recording, small transcription quirk.
[01:08] Leah Wong: On security: we need SOC2 level controls, audit logs, SSO integration (SAML/OIDC), and a procedure for key rotation. Also curious about log retention and access controls per-tenant.
[01:20] Zoe Alvarez: We typically support SSO/SCIM for onboarding, configurable retention windows, and audit logs — we can provide the SOC2 package. For private installs we also support HSM/KMS integrations.
[01:32] Carlos Ramirez: Commercially, we're thinking of a marketplace integration where Constellation resells a managed Redwood layer. What does the revenue share or marketplace arrangement typically look like?
[01:42] Maya Chen: We have a few models: standard hosted API reseller, dedicated/reserved capacity with a platform fee, or private OEM where we co-package an image and offer revenue share. Terms vary by commit size; we can send the partner one-pager with ranges.
[01:54] Ravi Patel: From a technical POV, we need to know what telemetry/metrics Redwood requires on the host side and whether we can surface those in our console. Also any per-token billing hooks so we can reconcile usage.
[02:06] Ethan Park: Yep — we emit token/latency/cost breakdowns per route. For private deploys we can ship Prometheus metrics and tracing hooks; for managed we provide a per-tenant usage feed and billing CSVs. Reconciliation via webhook or S3 dumps is possible.
[02:20] Anita Desai: About perf: what kind of quantization and kernel support do you require? We have mixed architectures and some nodes are older.
[02:28] Ethan Park: Redwood runtime chooses kernels based on architecture and sequence length distribution. We support int8 quantized variants and fallbacks to fp16. For older nodes we may suggest model variants or a dedicated pool. For initial pilot, we'd recommend running 1-2 representative models and sample traffic through a small dedicated pool to gather real QPS/latency numbers.
[02:48] Carlos Ramirez: Any vendor lock concerns? Partners want portability so we don't want to be stuck.
[02:54] Maya Chen: Portability is a core value — same API and configs across hosted, dedicated, and private. We don't require proprietary formats; we do help with model packaging and compatibility checks.
[03:04] Ravi Patel: On data residency — we have EU customers that require data to stay in-region. Can Redwood support region pinning in private deployments?
[03:11] Zoe Alvarez: Yes — for private we deploy in your region or on-prem, and for hosted we support region routing and data residency controls.
[03:18] Anita Desai: About benchmarking — what would you need from our side to run a perf evaluation?
[03:24] Ethan Park: We'll need sample models, representative prompts, and a list of node types and expected concurrency. We'll run two passes: a small synthetic workload to validate config, then a run with real samples to measure latency, throughput, and token costs. We'll share a perf worksheet.
[03:36] Leah Wong: For security review, we'll need your SOC2 report, pen test summary, and details on encryption-in-transit and at-rest. Also any data purging policies.
[03:44] Maya Chen: We can provide the SOC2 pack and a redacted pen test. For encryption we use TLS in transit and KMS/HSM options for at rest; we'll include specifics in the security doc.
[03:53] Carlos Ramirez: Competitors — we've looked at Lambda Labs for managed hosting and directly with AWS marketplace. How do you typically position vs those?
[04:01] Maya Chen: We position on production economics and cross-environment consistency. vs AWS marketplace we offer more turnkey inference controls and observability tailored to model serving; vs Lambda we emphasize enterprise features, rollouts/A-B, and predictable reserved pools.
[04:16] Ravi Patel: Sounds reasonable. For pilot sizing, we estimate 500 rps for lightweight embedding endpoints and 50 rps for chat generation. Is that within a normal pilot footprint?
[04:26] Ethan Park: Yes that's reasonable. For 500 rps embeddings we'd lean on batching and dedicated pools; we'll propose model/quantization settings in the worksheet.
[04:36] Anita Desai: One more ops question — how are KV caches shared or invalidated across multiple tenants if we run a mixed workload?
[04:42] Ethan Park: Cache is per-tenant and we have eviction policies and TTLs; multi-tenant cache sharing is discouraged for isolation reasons but we can discuss cross-tenant warmup strategies.
[04:54] Maya Chen: OK, wrapping up — recap: Redwood to send partner one-pager and pricing, Ethan sends perf worksheet and suggested configs, Constellation to share fleet inventory and security items. Plan to schedule a technical deep-dive the week of 2026-03-16.
[05:10] Carlos Ramirez: Perfect. We'll get the inventory and a security checklist to you by next week.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the docs and a Doodle for the deep-dive.
[05:22] (meeting ends)
